zh.summary: Stoa 是面向建筑项目的 AI 平台，从项目自有图纸、规格书、合同、进度和现场记录中检索并生成带引用的答案，辅助现场团队决策与产出。
zh.judgment: Stoa 以“只读接入现有系统、答案逐句引用原文”切入建筑项目信息碎片化痛点，但当前收入模式与单位经济尚未披露，商业验证仍待观察。
zh.replaces: 替代项目工程师在多个系统与文档间人工翻找条款、比对图纸版本、手工整理 RFI 与报告的低效流程。
zh.segment: 建筑项目信息管理与 AI 辅助决策
zh.product: Stoa 读取项目已有的图纸、规格书、合同、进度计划、质量检查与会议纪要，支持自然语言提问并逐句标注来源文档与页码。产品还提供图纸版本对比、变更追踪、项目总览、自动化检查以及将发现转化为报告、任务和可复用“技能”的能力。其范围覆盖从信息检索到工作产出的完整链路，但官网未披露模型细节与准确率基准。
zh.customer: 使用者是建筑项目上的工程师、项目经理、质量与安全负责人及现场团队；付费者可能是总承包商或项目业主方。痛点高频出现在图纸版本更新、RFI 答复、合同条款核对和检查整改等场景，官网称项目工程师每周可节省 2–8 小时，但该数字为公司披露，未经独立审计。
zh.workflow: Stoa 以只读方式同步 M-Files、SharePoint、Dalux、Congrid 等系统，保留原有权限，将图纸、规格书、合同、进度和检查记录汇入统一索引。用户用自然语言提问，系统返回带文档与页码引用的答案；发现变更后，可对比图纸版本、生成变更摘要，并将问题导出为报告、任务或保存为可复用的技能。官网称从签约到项目上线约两个工作日。
zh.business_model: 官网仅提示“询问定价”，未公开收费方式、单价或计费单位，因此无法判断是按项目、按用户还是按用量收费。单位经济推断缺乏依据，不能将融资额或项目价值当作收入证据。
zh.traction: 公司披露已在北欧二十多个项目上运行，覆盖数据中心、医院、住宅、铁路和改造项目，称覆盖项目价值超过 40 亿欧元，并有 40% 的项目价值运行在 Stoa 上。这些均为公司自述，缺少客户名单、留存率、付费转化与收入数据；案例页引用匿名项目经理的节省时间说法，不能作为审计结论。
zh.moat: 与通用大模型相比，Stoa 的差异在于只读接入项目系统、保留权限、逐句引用原文以及图纸版本对比等工程化能力；与旧流程相比，它把分散文档变成可检索、可追溯的工作流。壁垒取决于能否持续覆盖多系统集成、保持引用准确性，并让“技能”在项目间复用形成切换成本。
zh.funding_read: 本轮为 pre-seed，金额 350 万欧元，投资方包括 Lifeline Ventures、Wave Ventures、Illusian 及国际投资者；官网称由 Lifeline Ventures 领投。该阶段说明资金支持产品与早期项目部署，但不能证明需求验证或收入。资金用途未披露，下一里程碑应是公开定价、客户案例与留存指标。
zh.risks: 第一，若引用准确性不足或图纸解析出错，现场团队可能做出错误决策，导致信任崩塌。第二，建筑行业系统集成复杂、项目定制化程度高，若部署成本过高或无法规模化复制，单位经济难以成立。第三，通用模型厂商或现有项目管理软件增加类似功能，可能压缩其差异化空间。
zh.takeaway: Stoa 的做法值得借鉴：不重建客户系统，而是只读接入并保留权限；不追求全自动，而是让每条答案可追溯到原文；把一次性操作沉淀为可复用技能，降低项目间复制成本。
zh.watch_next: 下一阶段应关注：是否公开定价与计费单位；能否披露具名客户与留存率；引用准确率是否有第三方评估；以及从 pre-seed 到下一轮融资前，付费项目数量与收入是否可验证。

en.summary: Stoa is an AI platform for construction projects that answers questions from the project's own drawings, specifications, contracts, schedules and site records, with citations to the source document and page.
en.judgment: Stoa targets fragmented project information with read-only system integration and sentence-level citations, but its revenue model and unit economics are undisclosed, so commercial validation remains unproven.
en.replaces: Replaces manual searching across systems and documents for clauses, drawing revisions, RFIs and reports by project engineers.
en.segment: Construction project information management and AI-assisted decision support
en.product: Stoa reads existing drawings, specifications, contracts, schedules, quality inspections and meeting minutes, and supports natural-language questions with every sentence cited to its source document and page. It also offers drawing version comparison, change tracking, a project overview, automated checks, and the ability to turn findings into reports, tasks and reusable 'skills'. The scope covers information retrieval through work output, but model details and accuracy benchmarks are not disclosed.
en.customer: Users are project engineers, project managers, quality and safety leads, and site teams; payers are likely main contractors or project owners. High-frequency pain points include drawing revisions, RFI responses, contract clause checks and inspection follow-ups. The company claims 2–8 hours saved per project engineer per week, but this is company-reported and not independently audited.
en.workflow: Stoa syncs read-only from M-Files, SharePoint, Dalux, Congrid and other systems, preserving existing permissions, and indexes drawings, specifications, contracts, schedules and inspections. Users ask in natural language and receive answers with document and page citations; after changes are detected, users can compare drawing versions, generate change summaries, and export findings as reports, tasks or saved skills. The company claims about two working days from agreement to a live project.
en.business_model: The website only invites users to 'ask about pricing' and does not disclose pricing method, unit price or billing unit, so it is unclear whether pricing is per project, per user or usage-based. Unit economics cannot be inferred; funding amount or project value is not revenue evidence.
en.traction: The company reports running on more than twenty Nordic projects across data centres, hospitals, housing, rail and renovation, covering over €4 billion in project value, with 40% of project value running on Stoa. These are company-reported figures without customer names, retention, paid conversion or revenue data. Case examples quote anonymous project managers on time savings, which are not audit conclusions.
en.moat: Compared with general-purpose models, Stoa's differentiation lies in read-only integration with project systems, permission preservation, sentence-level citations and drawing version comparison. Compared with legacy workflows, it turns scattered documents into a searchable, traceable workflow. The moat depends on sustaining multi-system integrations, maintaining citation accuracy, and making 'skills' reusable across projects to create switching costs.
en.funding_read: This is a pre-seed round of €3.5 million from Lifeline Ventures, Wave Ventures, Illusian and international investors; the website says Lifeline Ventures led. The stage supports product development and early project deployments but does not prove demand validation or revenue. Use of funds is undisclosed; the next milestone should be public pricing, named customer cases and retention metrics.
en.risks: First, if citation accuracy or drawing parsing is insufficient, site teams could make wrong decisions, eroding trust. Second, construction system integration is complex and projects are highly customized; if deployment costs are high or replication fails, unit economics may not work. Third, general-purpose model vendors or existing project management software could add similar features, compressing differentiation.
en.takeaway: Stoa's approach offers lessons: integrate read-only with existing systems rather than rebuilding them; preserve permissions; make every answer traceable to source text rather than pursuing full automation; and turn one-off operations into reusable skills to lower cross-project replication costs.
en.watch_next: Next, watch whether Stoa discloses pricing and billing units; names customers and retention rates; provides third-party accuracy evaluations; and whether paid project count and revenue become verifiable before the next funding round.

evidence.text: Stoa develops an AI-powered platform that brings together drawings, schedules, and quality and safety reports to help construction teams manage project information, monitor progress, and coordinate operations across complex building sites.
